CHIEF COMPLAINT
Severe right upper arm pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
39-year-old female presenting with severe right upper arm and shoulder pain sustained during a volleyball game approximately 18 hours ago. Patient was attempting to spike the ball when she was kicked in the legs by an opponent, causing her to fall and land on her right shoulder/arm. Pain is rated 9/10 in severity. Patient has been taking ibuprofen every 6 hours with minimal relief. Has not used ice.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies numbness or tingling in right arm. Otherwise not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Gallstones
Lumbar fusion approximately 6 years ago

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen (every 6 hours)
Pepcid (for gallstones)

ALLERGIES
No allergies to medicines

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Plays volleyball

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right shoulder: swelling, erythema, and tenderness noted
Elbow: able to straighten and bend arm
Pulses: normal
Neurological: no numbness or tingling in right arm
General: rest of body normal

RESULTS
X-ray of right arm shows proximal humerus fracture

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Proximal humerus fracture. These fractures generally heal without surgery. Patient to be placed in long arm cast and sling for immobilization. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess bone realignment. If bones have not realigned, surgery will be considered at that time. Prescribed Lortab 5 mg, 1-2 tablets every 6 hours as needed for pain (20 tablets dispensed). Patient to proceed with casting.
